rules: Fields both scorers agree on are adopted unchanged.
The first run's written rules apply: margins judged at normal viewing size; halo, title, rock and corner glyphs count as lettering, conservatively.
Watercolor soft edges are recorded but do not make an image flawed (ADR 0006 amendment 2); a painted frame still does.
Unrequested, prominent figures count as extra figures, as in the first run.
noFormFigure no/na disputes resolve to no; neither is a figure.

scores.notes: Both independent scorers agree on every scored field. A: God appears only as smoke and light over the sanctuary (center-right). The two seraphim (upper center) are hooded human angels with just two wings each, not six, and no wings cover their faces or feet. The right seraph holds tongs with a burning coal, which belongs to v6, so the verse's defining six-wing image is missing.

Both independent scorers agree on every scored field. A: Bearded Ezekiel in undyed tunic and cloak stands center-left among a valley of skulls and bones, right hand outstretched, dust blowing at right; no God figure in the plain grey sky. Unrequested prop: he holds a blank wooden writing tablet and stylus in his left hand (center), no visible marks on it; painting reaches all four edges and corners are clean.

Both independent scorers agree on every scored field. A: Icon-style Moses and Aaron with plain gold halos before the camp, pig rooting mid-right, and God shown only as a faceless pillar of cloud over the tabernacle. Aaron's white headband (upper center-left) has a small dark curled scribble at its center that reads as a glyph-like inscription; edges are fully painted.

Both independent scorers agree on every scored field. A: Ink-and-watercolor: seated mother and child reaching toward rays breaking through cloud (center), terraced village, boats on lake (left), red-cloaked soldier and wood-carriers on road (right), grain basket (lower right); bottom-left and bottom-right corners soft-fade to white paper (style margin, not a flaw). Mother and child are larger than the requested small lower-third placement; a faint grey granulation smudge at the bottom edge near x~85% is not legible lettering.

Operator (matchesScene disputed): noFormFigure no/na: no figure either way; matchesScene takes the lower label. A: Boaz with plain, unmarked halo at left and lit doorway with lamps at right as requested; but a kneeling headscarfed woman lighting the lamps (center-right, by the doorway) is not in the present list and in Naomi's house reads as Ruth or Naomi, though the scene's 'lamps being lit' implies a lamp-lighter. No text in the halo, the shawl's zigzag band or the corners; painting reaches all four edges. B: Haloed Boaz stands at left with staff facing a lit doorway (plain halo, no marks; shawl hem has only geometric weave), but an unrequested young woman in a yellow veil kneels at center-right lighting the lamps and would read as Ruth or Naomi though only Boaz is in the scene's cast. All four edges are painted through; no lettering found.

Both independent scorers agree on every scored field. Halos are plain gold with no marks, gold ground runs to all four edges, no lettering in any corner.

Operator (extraFigures, overall disputed): A woman in a red maphorion leads a child to a bent old man: the group reads as Mary, the Christ child and Simeon, recurring figures the plan did not select (borderline). A: Icon-style courtyard with palm (left edge), whitewashed archway with hanging lamp (right), clay jars, a woman holding a child's hand at center and a Roman soldier at the right edge; painting reaches all four borders and the small paper in the red-robed man's hand (right) is blank. Villagers stand in a frontal frieze facing the viewer rather than turned toward the doorway in a half-circle, and the woman with child dominates the center. B: The central woman wears a red maphorion with the three Theotokos stars on forehead and shoulders and holds a child's hand while a bent old man with a staff reaches toward him (center), so the group reads as Mary, the Christ child and Simeon (a Presentation icon) rather than anonymous villagers. Most onlookers face the viewer instead of the doorway, and no reading is shown; the edges are fully painted and there is no lettering.

Both independent scorers agree on every scored field. Painting reaches all four edges; corners clean of marks.

Operator (noFormFigure disputed): noFormFigure no/na: no figure either way; matchesScene takes the lower label. The town is a larger walled city with a domed building rather than a village, a minor departure; edges are fully painted and there is no lettering.

Operator (matchesScene disputed): noFormFigure no/na: no figure either way; matchesScene takes the lower label. Job looks forward rather than up at the storm and the walled towns behind are intact rather than ruined; all four edges painted, no lettering.

Operator (edges disputed): Soft fade to white at the top corners (informational; soft Watercolor edges are not gated). A: Goliath (right) is upside-down in a cartwheel, head and hands at the ground and sandaled legs in the air, rather than falling forward on his face; he is barely larger than David. Both armies (left and right hills) are identical red-crested Greek hoplites, so the Israelites cannot be told apart. The watercolor wash fades to white paper at the top-left and top-right corners. David (left) follows through with the sling, armies line both hillsides, the white patch at top center is a painted sun glow rather than a margin, and shields carry no lettering.

Operator (coherence, overall disputed): Isaiah holds two separate staffs, and a seraph holds the coal from verse 6; both scorers saw both. But the left seraph already holds tongs with a burning coal (the later v.6 moment), both seraphim show bare uncovered feet against the verse, and Isaiah grips two separate staffs, one in each hand. B: Icon: Isaiah looks up from lower center at two winged seraphim above swirling incense smoke in a columned temple; no figure or face in the smoke or sanctuary. Seraphim show about four wings with bare feet uncovered, the left one holds tongs with a burning coal (from v.6), and Isaiah oddly grips two separate staffs; gold ground reaches all edges.

He walks down toward the viewer, away from the gate, and looks away from the mockers, so the 'going up' direction is not shown.

Operator (noFormFigure, matchesScene disputed): noFormFigure no/na: no figure either way; matchesScene takes the lower label. Both independent scorers agree on every scored field. A: A raised gold painted frame borders all four edges of the icon. Christ's cross-nimbus (upper right) carries Greek-style letters in its three arms. Operator (matchesScene disputed): noFormFigure no/na: no figure either way; matchesScene takes the lower label.
